chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us from a chain that he raised, saying: Al-Mufaddhal narrated to us from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

You are the people of Allah’s greeting and peace, and you are the people of Allah’s preference and mercy, and the people of Allah’s success and infallibility, and the people of Allah’s call and obedience. No reckoning will be upon you, nor fear, nor sorrow.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual privileges and promises for the faithful regarding divine mercy and the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Fadail al-Shia, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this narration to emphasize the unique spiritual status of the Shia as the exclusive recipients of divine greeting (Tahiyyat Allah) and protection (Ismah). The promise of exemption from detailed reckoning (Hisab) and absence of fear or sorrow underscores the concept of 'ease' in judgment for the faithful, a key theme in Shia eschatology. This reflects the belief that their adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt ensures divine favor and a direct path to salvation.
